title: Anthropic stock soars over 20% in Nasdaq debut
summary: Shares of Anthropic rose on their first day of trading, as investors weighted AI enthusiasm against a massive valuation and uncertain path to profitability.

image.caption: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 US per share late Wednesday, above the $70 to $78 US range stated by the company in recent regulatory filings. (REUTERS/Dado Ruvic)

blocks.text: Shares of Anthropic rose on their first day of trading, as investors weighted AI enthusiasm against a massive valuation and uncertain path to profitability.
Anthropic's IPO is the largest on record
Shares of Anthropic have started trading on the Nasdaq, rising over 20 per cent on the AI giant’s first day as a public company.

The stock debuted slightly before noon Eastern Time on Thursday, at $111.50 US per share, according to Bloomberg. That’s 34 per cent above the $83 US initial public offering (IPO) announced by the AI giant behind the popular Claude chatbot late Wednesday.
Shares are up 20.85 per cent, as of 12:27 p.m. ET.

Considered the first-ever pure-play artificial intelligence stock, Thursday’s public market debut pits AI enthusiasm directly against concerns among investors about the company’s massive valuation, and uncertain path to profitability.

Anthropic shares are now well above the $70 to $78 US range the company stated in recent regulatory filings earlier this month. On Wednesday, it boosted the number of shares up for sale, pushing its valuation slightly above $1.5 trillion US.
The San Francisco-based company holds the record for the largest-ever IPO, raising $81 billion US, well ahead of SpaceX, which raised about $75 billion US in June.

While Anthropic’s newly-minted stock is higher by double-digits today, the tech-heavy Nasdaq index is down slightly. AI-related stocks like Nvidia, Micron Technology and CoreWeave are also slipping lower.
Anthropic’s $1.5 trillion US valuation is but a drop in a bucket compared with the size of the opportunity it’s spelling out for investors.

In regulatory filings, Anthropic points to more than $40 trillion US in annual economic value generated by knowledge workers globally as the broader opportunity for its technology. The filing also cites industry estimates projecting that AI solutions will create $22.5 trillion US in cumulative economic impact by 2031
